status: source-only recommendation; no implementation, build, disassembly or runtime
recommendation: A narrow new bounded-run experiment remains justified. First replace per-block calls inside the already eligible C serial helper; optionally apply the same span calculation to the C-only pipeline branch. Retain all generic Swift loops, eligibility and reconstruction unchanged. Do not cherry-pick the historical pipeline wholesale over the current FMA256/empty-scratch fixes.
actualWorkRemoved: One Swift bridge call plus state construction/status switch per block becomes one per bounded span.
The 24-byte cursor/accumulator/available/marker wire value is imported/exported once per span; predictor stays local in C. Exact physical stores depend on compiler codegen.
C entrypoint pointer/count/precision/table/state guards are checked once per span; the unchanged per-block DC and AC bodies retain their error checks.
No coefficient zeroing, entropy work, dequantisation or Float arithmetic is omitted; no new image scratch/allocation.
scope: Existing 8/12-bit accelerated sequential greyscale with a successfully borrowed CDCTKernel only.
AC lookup requires at least512blocks, enough short-code coverage and a covered nonzero magnitude.
Tiny images, table-proven DC-only scans, unsupported/scalar paths, colour, progressive and lossless remain outside this route.

boundaries.runCount: min(rowEnd - index, restartInterval > 0 ? restartInterval - index % restartInterval : rowEnd - index)
boundaries.restartHandling: Swift skips/reset the marker before the span; no run crosses the next restart.
boundaries.cancellation: Keep NativeOperation.check at each existing outer row/group/batch boundary. The existing per-block C loop has no cancellation inside that segment. Run segmentation therefore does not extend any unpolled span; maximum256 blocks on FMA and1024 on GEMM.
boundaries.borrow: Run ends synchronously inside the same input/table/coefficient borrows. No entropy pointer enters a worker; publication/scatter/joins remain unchanged.

errorStateRequirements: Copy local cursor and predictor back on both success and entropy failure before Swift throws.
DC category or magnitude failure does not clear the failing coefficient slot or alter the predictor.
Accepted DC updates the predictor before AC; AC failure retains partial cleared/filled slot with slot0 still zero.
Range failure occurs after consuming DC but before predictor/slot publication.
Completed prior blocks remain written; the partial failing block matches scalar; later slots remain untouched.
Never signal or consume the incomplete window after an entropy failure; do not fall back after any input consumption.
Invalid counts/extent/precision reject before multiplication or any state/output write. Keep1...1024 and exact blocks*64 guards.
testNeeds: Port historical CDCTRunDecoderTests pure-Swift oracle and invalid-count/error-state tests; add255/256/257 alongside1/2/63/1024.
Repeat physical/logical cursor and next-read parity at all bit offsets, early/middle/last malformed DC/AC, stuffing and marker failures.
Extend current direct C serial tests to prove spans at256/1024 and restarts255/256/257/1023/1024.
Keep public8/12 integer/Float padded destination/copy assertions, joined cancellation/worker failure and zero-scratch TSan tests.
Fresh matched-source performance and full unrelated lossless controls required; historical held results establish no accepted gain for this new combination.

limitations: This is genuine call/state/check amortisation, not an established speedup. Dense AC and transform work can dominate, and restart1/very narrow rows offer little or no gain.
Historical C body refactoring and new call graph can change unrelated emitted code/layout; retain old single-block semantics and independently inspect both paths after any future build.
No current emitted-code/cycle/RSS conclusions are claimed.
